### GraphQL Specification Final Changes

The team discussed a final change to the GraphQL over HTTP specification, specifically replacing "recommended" with "should" in the language. Benjie explained the reasoning behind the change and made other minor clarifications to improve clarity. The group agreed to merge the specification with the suggested changes, though Leebyron noted one actionable comment that needed addressing regarding the extensions object. The team also discussed the timeline for releasing the specification in September, with Benjie indicating the changes should be landed within the next couple of days to start the 45-day countdown.

### Top-Level Properties Specification Discussion

The team discussed language around top-level properties in a specification, debating whether to use "must not" or "recommend" for adding additional properties. Benjie clarified that while adding top-level properties should be avoided, they should provide guidance on alternative approaches like using headers or extensions. The team agreed to frame the restriction more clearly as a "must not" and provide recommendations for when additional properties are necessary, with Benjie planning to either merge the current pull request as-is or make the suggested edits as a follow-up change.

### GraphQL Tagline Update Discussion

Martin reported on three active grants and mentioned that Alec is working on interactive tutorials for Houdini with plans to expand to other GraphQL stacks. Martin announced a new grant call for September and noted they have 13K remaining in the budget. The team discussed updating the GraphQL tagline to emphasize AI capabilities, with Martin having opened a pull request for a one-line website change. Leebyron suggested conducting a comprehensive search for all instances of the tagline to ensure it's updated everywhere, particularly in meta tags. Benjie raised concerns about the new tagline being less focused on GraphQL's core purpose compared to the previous version.

### On-Error Null Feature Proposal Discussion

Benjie presented an updated proposal for the on-error null feature, explaining how it would allow moving error propagation from server to client while making normalized caches safer. The discussion focused on whether to make this a default behavior or keep it as an opt-in, with Pascal emphasizing the importance of not changing defaults once implemented. The group agreed that new clients like Urkel and Apollo should default to using on-error null when supported by the server, while maintaining backward compatibility for older clients. Michael also proposed renaming the Composite Schema spec to GraphQL Federation spec to better reflect its evolution and alignment with Apollo Federation.
